events.title: POSIX.1 standardized
events.summary: [IEEE] published [POSIX].1 in September 1988 — standardizing Unix system call and C [API] interfaces for portable operating systems.
events.about: [POSIX] let developers write code that compiled on Solaris, AIX, Linux, and macOS without rewriting syscalls. It formalized what 'Unix-like' meant — shells, threads, and file I/O semantics that WSL and containers still emulate today.

narrative.whyChosen: [POSIX] unified the fragmented Unix vendor landscape under one portable [API].
narrative.whyImportant: It made cross-platform systems programming possible across commercial Unix and Linux.
narrative.problemSolved: Every Unix vendor shipped incompatible libc and syscall variants.
